To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) distal PA-SM are phenotypically homogeneous and highly differentiated, and 2) distal PA exhibit distinct patterns of DNA synthesis in vitro that are different from proximal PA.
distal PA media are composed of a phenotypically uniform population of well differentiated SMC that are resistant to proliferation and have a substantial ability to hypertrophy in vitro.

the media of the normal distal bovine pulmonary artery is composed of a homogeneous population of well-determined SMC that are growth-inhibited by hypoxia and that differ from SMC in the media of the proximal pulmonary artery in their proliferative response to serum and growth factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of smooth muscle cells ( SMC ) in the pulmonary arteries.
the role of smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotype in the regulation of vascular growth in the pulmonary circulation.
the characterization of the pulmonary artery smooth muscle phenotype and its relationship with the pulmonary circulation in health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the media of the distal PA is composed of a well-differentiated population of SMC that exhibit low proliferative capabilities in contrast to proximal PA SMC.
the SMC phenotype of distal PA is distinct from that of MPA, and this may be of importance in the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension.

the media of the distal PA (100-1,500 microm diameter) is a homogeneous population of "well differentiated" SMC that are growth resistant but exhibit substantial hypertrophic responses to growth-promoting agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the media of the bovine main pulmonary arteries (MPA) and distal pulmonary arteries are composed of phenotypic heterogeneous and homogeneous smooth muscle cells (SMA), respectively.
distal SMC are phenotypically and functionally distinct from proximal PA-SMC and that these characteristics may be important in regulating the pulmonary circulation.
distal pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells are more differentiated, and thus less proliferative, than proximal pulmonary artery smooth muscle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the media of the distal pulmonary artery is composed of a homogeneous population of differentiated smooth muscle cells that are proliferation resistant.
the pulmonary vascular smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotype is not uniform along the proximal-distal axis.
the media of normal distal pulmonary arteries is composed of a homogeneous population of well-distinguished SMC that are resistant to growth stimulation by mitogens and serum.
